heading: Which languages can I use?
summary: You can write a Tac service in the supported languages below. Lua and Python are supported with limits. C++ is in progress, and other WebAssembly languages are not supported.
body:
A Tac service is a class in `client/services`. Tachyon reads that class, connects its fields, methods, events and storage to the page, and runs its test units. A language is a Tac service language only when Tachyon does all of this for it. A compiler that makes WebAssembly is not enough. Each language below is in one of four groups.

Supported and tested: JavaScript and TypeScript run in the page as JavaScript. Rust, Go, C#, F#, Swift, Kotlin, Java, Dart and Ruby run in the page as WebAssembly. Tachyon tests each of these languages with its own test units and in a real browser. The feature pages show examples in them, and the site build checks those examples. When one of these languages cannot use a feature, the feature page says so and names the build error.

Supported with limits: Lua and Python work, but some features are not ready in them yet. Each feature page says when Lua or Python cannot use the feature.

Lua runs on Tachyon's Lua 5.4 WebAssembly runtime (ADR 0085; an ADR is an architecture decision record). A Lua service has fields, methods, `OnStart` and `OnStop`, events with `ApplicationEventPublisher` and `OnEvent`, test units, and Tachyon's browser APIs except `WindowControls`. The build refuses these in Lua with `TY1308`: behavior annotations such as `Cached`, `Retry` and `AllOrNothing`, `HTTPClient`, `Store`, `LocalState`, `SessionState`, `Topic`, `Helper` and `Fake`.

Python runs on Pyodide 314.0.7, a Python runtime for WebAssembly (ADR 0093). A Python service has fields, methods, models, `Needs`, `NeedsAll`, `Named`, helpers, synchronous `on_start` and `on_stop`, and test units. Every call is synchronous. An `async def` method, an event listener or a stream stops the build with `TY1605`. `HTTPClient`, `Store` and `Topic` stop the build with `TY1308`. Behavior annotations such as `Cached` and `Retry` need an `async def` method, so Python cannot use them yet. Python has no browser APIs and no saved `LocalState` or `SessionState` fields yet. ADR 0093 covers web builds; Tachyon does not test Python services in native apps.

In progress and planned: you cannot use these languages today, and the plan can change. C++ is in progress: Tachyon is adding C++ services that Emscripten compiles to WebAssembly. Zig is planned. Scala, through the WebAssembly output of Scala.js, and MoonBit, after its version 1.0, are under consideration.

Not supported: many other languages can reach a browser through WebAssembly, for example Haskell, OCaml, Grain, Nim, D, Odin, Crystal, AssemblyScript, Elixir, PHP, Perl and R. Tachyon does not support them as Tac service languages, and you cannot write a Tac service in them. Some languages compile to JavaScript, not to WebAssembly, for example Gleam, Elm and ClojureScript. Tachyon does not support them as Tac service languages either. A server language such as PHP can still be a Yon language (see The Yon languages).

The table shows how each language runs. Calls says whether the page waits for a method. Native host says where a native app links the service in; everywhere else the service runs in the page, also inside a native app. `HTTPClient` says how a client in that language sends requests (see Calling the server from a page). Example names a working service in Code examples on the home page; the site build compiles and checks each one.

| Language | Group | Runs as | Toolchain | Calls | Native host | `HTTPClient` | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| JavaScript | Supported and tested | JavaScript in the page | none | Synchronous or `async` | none | sent by the browser | `TallyService.js` |
| TypeScript | Supported and tested | JavaScript in the page, after `tsc` | TypeScript 6 or newer | Synchronous or `async` | none | sent by the browser | `TallyService.ts` |
| Rust | Supported and tested | WebAssembly (`wasm32-unknown-unknown`) | rustc 1.97.1 | Synchronous; an `async fn` runs on Tachyon's task runner in the module | macOS, Windows and Linux | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.rs` |
| Go | Supported and tested | WebAssembly (`GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm`) | Go 1.27 or newer; TinyGo 0.42 or newer is optional and makes release modules smaller | Each call runs in a goroutine; a call that waits finishes later | none | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.go` |
| C# | Supported and tested | WebAssembly on the trimmed .NET browser runtime | .NET SDK 9.0.317 (`net9.0`) with the `wasm-tools` workload | Synchronous; a `Task` method is awaited | Windows | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.cs` |
| F# | Supported and tested | WebAssembly on the same .NET browser runtime as C# | the same .NET SDK as C# | Synchronous; a `Task` method is awaited | none | sent by the browser | `TallyService.fs` |
| Swift | Supported and tested | WebAssembly (`wasm32-unknown-wasip1`) | Swift 6.3.3 from swift.org and its Swift SDK for WebAssembly, found through `TAC_SWIFT_WASM_SDK` | Synchronous; an `async` method runs to the end before the call returns | macOS and iOS | through the Setup's HTTP adapter | `TallyService.swift` |
| Kotlin | Supported and tested | WebAssembly with garbage collection (WasmGC) | kotlinc 2.1.10 and kotlin-stdlib-wasm-js 2.1.10, found through `TAC_KOTLIN_WASM_STDLIB` | Synchronous | Android | through the Setup's HTTP adapter | `TallyService.kt` |
| Java | Supported and tested | WasmGC, made by TeaVM | JDK 21 or newer and TeaVM 0.15.0 | Synchronous | none | through the Setup's HTTP adapter | `TallyService.java` |
| Dart | Supported and tested | WasmGC (`dart compile wasm`) | Dart SDK 3.13 or newer | Synchronous; a `Future` method is awaited | none | sent by the browser, through `Needs` | `TallyService.dart` |
| Ruby | Supported and tested | Tachyon's mruby WebAssembly runtime | Ruby and Emscripten 6.0.10 build the pinned mruby once on your machine | Synchronous; `sleep` is refused | none | through the Setup's HTTP adapter | `TallyService.rb` |
| Lua | Supported with limits | Tachyon's Lua 5.4.9 WebAssembly runtime, about 170 KB | Emscripten 6.0.10 builds it once on your machine | Synchronous | none | no; the build refuses it (`TY1308`) | `TallyService.lua` |
| Python | Supported with limits | Pyodide 314.0.7 (CPython 3.14.2), about 13 MB before compression | the five pinned Pyodide files, which you put in the Tachyon cache | Synchronous only; `async def` stops the build (`TY1605`) | none | no; the build refuses it (`TY1308`) | `TallyService.py` |
| C++ | In progress | not available yet | not available yet | not available yet | not available yet | not available yet | none yet |

Kotlin, Java and Dart need a browser with WasmGC: Chrome or Edge 119, Firefox 120, Safari 18.2 or newer. An older browser shows a clear error instead of these services. `ty doctor` lists the tools that your project needs and says which ones are missing. A page loads the runtime of a language only when one of its views uses a service in that language.
